## Reasoning

The request asks me to "just output 20 columns and configs," but doing so blindly would hide two decisions that determine whether the study answers anything. I'll respect the intent (concrete, enumerated columns + a shared ELM config are included below) while keeping the strategy honest.

**Decomposition.** The stated goal is water partitioning (ET vs. surface runoff vs. subsurface drainage) and its drivers across the Naches (HUC 17030002), a high-relief basin (352–1977 m). Candidate drivers are elevation and soil. There is a second, implicit goal — validation — but `observations_available` is empty, so there is **nothing in-domain to validate against**. That is a real gap, not something I can design around.

**Feasibility of the drivers.** Naches is in CONUS, so the default NLDAS-2 forcing (~12 km) applies: precipitation and temperature *do* vary orographically across a 1600 m-relief basin, so an elevation-stratified column set will see a genuine (if coarse) climate/snow gradient — this is answerable, unlike the out-of-CONUS case. The limit: sub-12 km terrain is unresolved, so adjacent high columns may share a cell and ridgetop SWE will be underestimated. Soil (SSURGO, per-column) is fully answerable. Because the drivers include snow-zone behavior and subsurface drainage, the design needs snow output (default) and **spin-up / WTD warm start** so soil-moisture and drainage aren't cold-start artifacts.

**N and placement.** All 20 are exploratory (no validation points possible). I stratify elevation × soil and oversample the rain–snow transition (~1200–1500 m), where snowmelt timing most strongly reshapes partitioning. Columns are placed on a west (Cascade crest, high) → east (Naches valley, low) gradient.

**Verdict: partial** — soil and coarse orographic-elevation controls on partitioning are answerable; validation is not (no in-domain data), and fine-scale elevation/snow is only coarsely resolved.
